artboards.title: B · One slot at a time
C · The ship is the page

annotations.text: Shared fix across all three: the currency is build credits, gold chips in a tray under the head. Free chips are solid, spent ones are sockets, and every price is drawn as the chips it costs. No numerals, no blue bar, no explainer sentences.

A keeps the list but quiets it: a row is slot, setting, price. Triangles only on the row you are standing on, at full row height, so mouse, tap and d-pad all hit them. Closest to what ships; still the wordiest of the three.

B holds one slot at a time and draws what it does. Left and right walk the slots, minus and plus are the whole interface, the plus key wears its price. Calmest and best on a phone or pad; costs a press per slot to survey the build.

C has no list: the build is the ship firing it, and each drawn cluster is its own control, stepped inside the gold brackets. Most legible at a glance and the most fun; the add-ons without an obvious drawing (freeze, fuse) need one invented.
The open fork: whether flight is spendable too. This board sketches that side. The recommendation is no, so ships stay ships; the points live in gun, bomb and rack.
The first pass, kept for reference: sentences stepped by triangles, numeral prices, the budget as a bar. Chris's read: busy, the numbers and the bar opaque. The Options page is the answer.
